findings:
🟠 [oracle-modified] MUST-FIX The depth-0-owned acceptance oracle `packages/relay/tests/adversarial/groups.test.ts` is modified, and the diff also changes disallowed pre-existing `fanout.test.ts`; this invalidates the supplied verification evidence and violates the frozen harness boundary. Revert all unauthorized test changes and make the implementation pass the original oracle.
🟠 [read-scope-in-js] MUST-FIX `grants.ts` and `replies.ts` fetch reply routes globally before checking membership in JavaScript; existing cross-group IDs therefore execute additional queries compared with nonexistent IDs, creating the forbidden timing/existence distinction and violating SQL-WHERE enforcement. Scope route retrieval with a `group_member`/`since_msg_id` SQL predicate so inaccessible and nonexistent IDs follow the same lookup path.
🟠 [send-validation-order] MUST-FIX `in_reply_to` validation remains inside `buildEnvelope`, which is called only after address-rule and subject-ACL refusals; requests with an inaccessible parent can therefore return those earlier errors instead of the required group-scoped parent result. Perform the group-scoped parent lookup before address rules and subject ACL, preserving the specified validation order.
🟠 [refusal-audit-group] MUST-FIX Several strict-mode refusals are unaudited or omit `group_id`, including `idempotency_mismatch`, `not_in_thread`, and the visible subject-denial audit calls. This violates the requirement that every refusal be audited with its group. Route all refusal exits through auditing that records the resolved `group_id`.
